sentences.text: Bench: Abhay S. Oka  IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA  CRIMINAL APPELLATE JURISDICTION  CRIMINAL APPEAL NOS.544-547 OF 2022  BRITANNIA INDUSTRIES LIMITED ... APPELLANT(S)

VS.
 STATE OF UTTAR PRADESH & ANR.ETC. ...
RESPONDENT(S  O R D E R Heard the learned senior counsel appearing for the appellant.

By the impugned order, four petitions filed by the appellant for quashing the prosecution for the offence punishable under Section 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (for short "the PFA Act") were dismissed.
The allegation in the complaints was of misbranding, in the sense, that there was a violation of Rule 32(e) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955 (for short "the PFA Rules").

Rule 32(e) and 32(f) read thus:
"Rule 32(e) A distinctive batch number or lot number or code number, either in numericals or alphabets or in combination, the numericals or alphabets or their combination, representing the batch number or lot number or code number being preceded by the words "Batch No." or Batch or 17:27:25 IST "Lot No." or "Lot" or any distinguishing prefix:
Provided that in case of canned food, the batch number may be given at the bottom,
or on the lid of the container, but the words "Batch No." given at the bottom or on the lid, shall appear on the body of the container.
(f) the month and year in which the commodity is manufactured or prepacked;
Provided also that in case of carbonated water containers and the packages of biscuits, confectionery and sweets, containing more than 60g. but not more than 120 g. and food packages weighing not Britannia Industries Limited vs The State Of Uttar Pradesh on 29 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/8501887/
1 more than 60 g. particulars under clauses (d) and (e) need not be specified;"

sentences.text: The first submission of the learned senior counsel appearing for the appellant is that Rule 32(e) in its earlier form was struck down by this Court in the case of Dwarka Nath & Anr. v. Municipal Corporation of Delhi1.

entities.text: Dwarka Nath & Anr. v. Municipal Corporation of Delhi1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: His first submission is that the issue of validity of the amended rule on the basis of which the appellant was sought to be prosecuted was urged before the High Court.
He submits that the law laid down by this Court in the case of Dwarka Nath1 will squarely apply to the Rule 32(e) in its new form.

In the alternative, his submission is that there was a policy of the Government of Delhi that in case of first violation of the Rule 32(e), before filing the complaint, a notice is required to be served to the offender giving him an opportunity to rectify.
He submitted that on the basis of the said 1. (1971) 2 SCC 314 policy, a large numbers of complaints have been quashed by the Delhi High Court.
Having considered the submissions, we find that no relief can be granted in these appeals.
The first reason is that there was no challenge to the validity of the Rule 32(e) of the PFA Rules in the petitions filed under Section 482 of the Criminal Procedure Code, 1973.
Moreover, the Union of India which has framed the PFA Rules was not made a party either before the High Court or before this Court.
There is one more reason.
A perusal of the impugned judgment shows that the argument by the appellant was not that the Rule 32(e) in its new form is ultra vires.
The specific argument made was that in view of the decision of this Court in the case of Dwarka Nath1, the amended rule could not have been applied to the case of the appellant.
The petitions for quashing are of the year 2005 and 2008.
Now, it is too late in the day now to permit amendment for impleading the Union of India as a party.

So far as the second point urged is concerned, if a policy similar to the policy applicable to the State of Delhi has been framed by the respondent-State of Uttar Pradesh, the appellant can always rely upon the said policy before the Trial Court.
Therefore, there is no reason to interfere with the impugned order.
Accordingly, the appeals are dismissed subject to what is observed above.
We also make it clear that we have made no adjudication on the issue of the validity of the Rule 32(e) of the PFA Rules as amended .
All issues in the pending complaints are left open.

..........................J. (ABHAY S.OKA) ..........................J. (UJJAL BHUYAN) NEW DELHI;
February 29, 2024.
